newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Fifth British soldier charged with Cyprus attack.
newsitem.headline: Fifth British soldier charged with Cyprus attack.

text.p: Cyprus police charged a fifth British soldier on Wednesday in connection with an attack on a group of British holidaymakers at a popular tourist resort at the weekend.
Stuart Spencer, 20, was charged with instigating an attack on three British tourists and released into the custody of the British military base authorities on the holiday island.

Spencer will appear before a Cyprus court on Thursday morning with fellow soldiers Roger Bell, 26, Tim Carter, 20, Steven Wolstencroft, 26, and Steven Girvan, 20, a spokesman for the British bases said.
The soldiers face charges of causing grievous bodily harm to Shane Bell and Barry Ford, both 23, and actual bodily harm to Claire Harbour, 22, all from south-east London.
Spencer was charged after the tourists picked him out during an identity parade in the car park at Ayia Napa police station. The four other soldiers were arrested over the weekend.
All five are members of the First Battalion, Kings Regiment, stationed at the British base of Dhekelia.
The British army has banned all 600 members of the regiment from entering the sprawling south eastern resort of Ayia Napa, where the attack took place outside a disco early on Saturday morning.
Some 3,500 British troops are stationed at two military bases Britain has retained in Cyprus since independence in 1960.
